home.eyebrow: Bioelectric Field Research · Electroporation · Resonance Modeling
home.subtitle: Virtual Biophysics Engine
home.taglineMain: Set an RF frequency, watch the transmembrane voltage climb in real time, and find the precise window where a cancer cell reaches lysis threshold while the healthy cell beside it remains sub-threshold. Built on the Schwan equation, Pennes bioheat model, nsEP pulse-envelope physics, and the Clausius-Mossotti DEP force model, export publication-ready parameters before running a single in-vitro experiment.
home.wf1Desc: Pick any of 10 presets, cancer lines, bacteria, viruses, or healthy reference, and pair a target against a healthy baseline.
home.wf2Desc: Set frequency, field intensity, waveform, duty cycle, and pulse width. Watch transmembrane voltage, disruption ratio, and temperature update live.
home.wf3Desc: Sweep parameters to find the therapeutic window, monitor impedance drift, and export a full Methods section for your publication.
home.card1Desc: Live Schwan Vm, disruption ratios, SAR temperature, frequency response chart, field & frequency sweep, and cell population distribution, all in one workspace.
home.card2Desc: Tracks cuvette impedance as cells lyse, computes corrected generator voltage, and sonifies live physics data via the Web Audio API.
home.card3Desc: Log readings and lysis events. Select any entry to export a publication-ready Materials and Methods section with full cell parameters, exposure protocol, and literature references.
home.card4Desc: 16 biologically-grounded presets: 5 reference cells (hepatocyte, RBC, astrocyte, fibroblast, lymphocyte), 7 cancer lines, E. coli, MRSA, Influenza A, and SARS-CoV-2, with computed Cm, τ, fc, and DEP crossover frequency f_cross.
home.card5Desc: Full derivations for Schwan Vm, SAR, Lorentzian resonance, nsEP pulse selectivity, DEP Clausius-Mossotti model, impedance feedback, and sonification, plus a 12-step experimental guide.
home.ctaRefs: Built on Kotnik & Miklavcic 2000 · Pennes 1948 · Weaver & Chizmadzhev 1996
home.tipSciCell: Schwan equation: Vm = 1.5 E R cos(θ) / √(1+(ωτ)²). Cyan ions drift toward the +Vm pole, red toward -Vm, building the transmembrane potential that drives electroporation. Click to explore in the lab.
home.tipSciChart: Vm rolls off above the characteristic frequency fc = 1/(2πτ). Below fc the membrane fully charges; above fc it stays sub-threshold. The animated dot shows the current operating point. Click to tune parameters.
home.disclaimer: for research visualisation only · not a medical device
